Read an article some time ago (still trying to remember where to post cite- sorry).....article described that commercials "sound" louder than shows is that they adjust the volume to have all audio at highest permitted level....think any Michael Bey movie with all dialogue at some volume as the explosions...

As I recall a Federal law was passed that they had to be the same volume. The networks then found away to "compress" (that was the word that was used in the article I read, don't ask me to explain) the commercials so they would still be louder. Another federal law was passed but the networks found a way around it again.

The secret is compression. Your show has dynamics in volume. Probably ranging from -24dBFS (silence) to -6dBFS. Dialogue is typically around -12 to -8dBFS. Commercials are pinned at -6 to 0dBFS using compression/limiting. They "limit" everything (music, talking, sfx) to go as "loud" as possible. It's called "limiting" because you can (usually responsibly) set a "limit" to how loud it should go. They set it to -6dBFS, because that's their legal limit.
